section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which agency handles driver licensing and permits in Massachusetts?
options: a:Massachusetts DMV,b:Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV),c:Massachusetts DOT,d:Massachusetts Secretary of State
note: Massachusetts's Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) handles driver licensing, vehicle registration, and permits. Massachusetts does not have a traditional DMV — the RMV is the licensing authority in the state.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Massachusetts's real RMV knowledge test has 25 questions. How many must you get right to pass — and what makes this threshold unusual?
options: a:22 correct (88%) — higher than most states,b:20 correct (80%) — same as most states,c:18 correct (72%) — lower than most states,d:15 correct (60%) — much lower than most states
note: Massachusetts requires only 18 out of 25 correct — a 72% passing threshold. This is lower than the 80% standard used by most other states. You can miss up to 7 questions and still pass. While the bar is lower, don't treat this as a reason to under-prepare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How many questions can you miss on Massachusetts's RMV knowledge test and still pass?
options: a:3 questions (88% threshold),b:5 questions (80% threshold),c:7 questions (72% threshold),d:10 questions (60% threshold)
note: You can miss up to 7 questions on Massachusetts's 25-question test and still pass at 72%. This is more lenient than the typical 80% standard. However, fully understanding the rules of the road matters for your safety long after the test.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Massachusetts learner's permit?
options: a:15,b:16,c:15 and a half,d:14
note: Massachusetts requires applicants to be at least 16 years old to apply for a learner's permit. This is older than many other states, which allow permits at 15 or even 14. Massachusetts also requires completion of an approved driver education program before getting a junior operator's license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a Massachusetts driver age 21 or older?
note: Massachusetts sets the OUI (Operating Under the Influence) limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Massachusetts uses the term OUI rather than DUI. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Massachusetts uses the term 'OUI' for drunk driving. What does OUI stand for?
options: a:Operating Under Influence,b:Operating Under Intoxication,c:Offense Under Impairment,d:Operating Unfit Impaired
note: Massachusetts uses OUI — Operating Under the Influence — rather than DUI or DWI. The concept is the same: operating a motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol or drugs, or with a BAC of 0.08% or higher for drivers 21 and older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What BAC triggers Massachusetts's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21?
note: Massachusetts sets the underage OUI threshold at 0.02% BAC for drivers under 21 — effectively zero. Any measurable amount of alcohol above 0.02% is illegal for drivers under 21 in Massachusetts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Massachusetts's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a permit holder log?
options: a:30 hours (no night requirement),b:40 hours (10 at night),c:40 hours (no specific night requirement),d:50 hours (10 at night)
note: Massachusetts requires 40 hours of supervised driving practice, with at least 10 hours driven at night. The supervising driver must be a licensed adult age 21 or older seated in the front seat. These hours must be certified before applying for a junior operator's license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on Massachusetts urban streets when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:45 mph
note: Massachusetts sets the default speed limit in thickly settled districts (urban areas) at 30 mph when no sign is posted. On rural roads, the default is 50 mph. Always check for posted signs — use defaults only when no sign is visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is Massachusetts's default speed limit on rural roads — and how does it differ from most states?
options: a:55 mph — same as most states,b:50 mph — slightly lower than most states' 55 mph,c:65 mph — higher than most states,d:45 mph — significantly lower than most states
note: Massachusetts's default rural road speed limit is 50 mph — slightly lower than the 55 mph default used by most other states. Massachusetts's more dense and older road infrastructure contributed to this lower default limit. Always check for posted speed limit signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Massachusetts's Move Over law requires what when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a:Slow to 25 mph only,b:Move one lane away if safe, or reduce speed if a lane change is not possible,c:Stop completely behind the vehicle,d:Only applies to police vehicles
note: Massachusetts's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from stationary emergency, law enforcement, utility, or tow vehicles with flashing lights. If a safe lane change is not possible, significantly reduce speed. The law applies to all such vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must Massachusetts drivers use their headlights?
options: a:Only from sunset to sunrise,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and when visibility is under 500 feet,c:Only in rain and fog,d:Only after 9 PM
note: Massachusetts requires headlights from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise, and whenever weather reduces visibility to less than 500 feet. This includes rain, fog, and snow — not just complete darkness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach a school bus stopped on an undivided road with red flashing lights. What must you do?
options: a:Stop only if you are behind the bus,b:Stop in both directions at least 100 feet from the bus,c:Slow to 15 mph and proceed carefully,d:Stop only if children are visible
note: Massachusetts law requires all vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 100 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights. Wait until the stop arm retracts and lights stop before proceeding. On a divided highway, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum recommended following distance in Massachusetts under normal conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Massachusetts recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In rain, fog, or on wet roads, increase to at least 6 seconds. Given Massachusetts's heavy traffic and stop-and-go city driving, maintaining adequate following distance is especially important.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Yield to cross traffic and proceed,c:Come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe,d:Continue at the posted speed
note: A flashing red signal is treated exactly like a stop sign in Massachusetts. Make a complete stop, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe. A flashing yellow means caution — slow down but a full stop is not required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road in Massachusetts, when may you cross a solid yellow center line to pass?
options: a:When the road ahead is visible for at least 500 feet,b:You may never cross a solid yellow line on your side to pass,c:When the vehicle ahead is traveling below the speed limit,d:When you signal for at least 200 feet first
note: A solid yellow line on your side prohibits crossing the center line to pass. No exceptions. Only when a broken (dashed) yellow line is on your side may you pass when it is safe. Always verify the line type on your side before attempting to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Massachusetts seatbelt law requires which occupants to wear a seatbelt?
options: a:Driver and front-seat passengers only,b:All occupants,c:Only those under 16,d:Driver only
note: Massachusetts requires all vehicle occupants — in all seating positions — to wear a seatbelt. Massachusetts has primary enforcement. Children must use appropriate child safety seats based on age and size.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must:
options: a:Speed up and move out of the way quickly,b:Pull to the right edge and stop,c:Slow to 15 mph in your lane,d:Move to the center lane
note: Massachusetts law requires you to immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches. Remain stopped until the vehicle passes. If in an intersection, clear it first, then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you make a right turn on a red light in Massachusetts?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if the turn is clear,d:Only on one-way streets
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Massachusetts after a complete stop, yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic, and unless a 'No Turn on Red' sign is posted. Always make a full stop — rolling through on red is illegal even when turning right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a vehicle to your right. Who goes first?
options: a:You go first,b:The vehicle on your right goes first,c:Whoever is going straight has priority,d:The larger vehicle goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a 4-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right of way. You must yield to the driver on your right. This is the standard tie-breaking rule used at all-way stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Massachusetts rural interstate highways?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Massachusetts's maximum speed limit on rural interstate highways is 65 mph for passenger vehicles. This is lower than many other states. Some urban sections may have lower posted limits. Always check posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Massachusetts requires Junior Operator License (JOL) holders to follow GDL restrictions. What is the nighttime driving curfew for a JOL holder?
options: a:No curfew — JOL holders may drive at any time,b:No driving between midnight and 5 AM (unless accompanied by a licensed adult),c:No driving between 1 AM and 5 AM (unless accompanied by a licensed adult),d:No driving after 11 PM
note: Massachusetts Junior Operator License (JOL) holders under 18 may not drive between midnight and 5 AM unless accompanied by a licensed adult 21 or older. During the first 6 months of the JOL, no passengers under 18 are allowed unless they are family members.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian is crossing in a marked crosswalk. You must:
options: a:Proceed if you have a green light,b:Slow to 15 mph and proceed carefully,c:Stop and yield until the pedestrian has completely crossed the roadway,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is in your lane
note: Massachusetts law requires stopping and yielding to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must remain stopped until the pedestrian has completely cleared the roadway — even with a green light. Pedestrian right-of-way in a crosswalk is absolute.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Massachusetts law requires drivers to signal before turning at least how far in advance?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:150 feet,d:200 feet
note: Massachusetts law requires drivers to signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. On higher-speed roads, earlier signaling is advisable. Failing to signal or signaling too late is illegal and potentially dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if your vehicle's accelerator becomes stuck while driving?
options: a:Slam the brakes as hard as possible immediately,b:Shift to neutral, apply steady brake pressure, and safely steer to the side of the road,c:Turn off the ignition immediately,d:Accelerate to blow out the engine
note: If your accelerator sticks, shift to neutral — this disengages the engine from the wheels — then apply steady brake pressure and steer safely to the side of the road. This sequence maintains steering control while reducing speed. Slamming brakes at high speed without shifting can cause skidding.

question: Motorists should remember that large trucks:
options: a:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,b:Require less space to turn than cars.,c:Have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots (no-zones) along the sides, rear, and sometimes front of the vehicle. They also need more distance to stop and more space to turn or change lanes. Give them extra room and avoid lingering alongside them where the driver may not see you.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, you should:
options: a:Assume a door may open and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Brake hard and sound your horn.
note: When passing a parked vehicle, always expect that a door could open or someone could step out suddenly. Slow slightly if needed, leave as much space as you safely can, and be prepared to brake. Do not speed up or rely on the horn; focus on space and time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down before you reach the exit ramp.,b:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant while on the ramp.,d:Stop at the start of the ramp and then slow down.
note: On freeways, maintain your speed until you are actually in the exit lane and on the ramp, then slow down as needed. Braking on the main freeway lane can surprise drivers behind you and cause rear-end collisions. Use the ramp area to reduce speed safely to the posted advisory speed.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross at your own risk if signals are off.,d:Speed up to clear the tracks before it arrives.
note: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Trains cannot stop quickly, and they always have the right-of-way. Wait until the train has completely passed and any gates, lights, or bells show that it is safe before crossing.

question: When driving in bad weather you should:
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Increase speed to reach your destination sooner.
note: In bad weather, roads can become slippery and visibility may be reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Increase your following distance so you have a longer stopping distance and can brake gently to avoid skids or rear-end collisions.

question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and oncoming traffic blocks your view, you should:
options: a:Wave oncoming drivers to let you go.,b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning.,c:Accelerate rapidly as soon as the first lane clears.
note: Before making a left turn, you must be able to clearly see all lanes you will cross and be sure they are free of oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards. If your view is blocked, wait with your wheels straight until you can see that it is safe to complete the turn.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A steady green light.,d:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians. Unlike a flashing red, you are not required to stop, but you must be prepared to yield if necessary.

question: When it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance.,b:Maintain normal following distance and drive as usual.,c:Speed up to get to your destination sooner.
note: When it starts to sleet or snow, visibility and traction both decrease. Keep your windshield and mirrors clear, turn on your lights, and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to stop on the slippery surface.

question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must the driver produce?
options: a:Proof of insurance only.,b:Your driver’s license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.,c:Proof of vehicle registration only.
note: When stopped, the driver must be prepared to produce their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance; carrying all three is required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the other vehicle.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Enter the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.,d:Honk to assert your right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slow down, let that driver go first, and then proceed when the way is clear.

question: If you are involved in a crash, what is your first responsibility at the scene?
options: a:Stop your vehicle immediately and remain at the scene.,b:Immediately leave the scene and report later.,c:Drive to the nearest police station before helping.,d:Continue driving if damage appears minor.
note: After any crash, you must stop immediately and stay at the scene. Once stopped and safe, you should move your vehicle out of traffic if possible, call emergency services, exchange information, and help anyone who is injured without moving them unless there is immediate danger.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest rule when vehicles are approaching a crosswalk?
options: a:Always insist on your right-of-way and step into traffic.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk while vehicles are approaching closely.,c:Assume drivers will always stop for you.,d:Cross at any point regardless of vehicle distance.
note: Even when you have the right-of-way in a crosswalk, you should not step into the street if vehicles are approaching so closely or quickly that they cannot stop safely. Make eye contact with drivers, wait until it is clear they are stopping, and then cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane closest to your original lane.,d:Turn and immediately change into any lane you prefer.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane road, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you are coming from. This keeps traffic organized and prevents side-swipe collisions. Complete the turn first, then change lanes only when it is safe and legal.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your front wheels away from the curb.,b:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.,c:Keep the rear tires tight against the curb.,d:Turn your front wheels toward the curb.
note: Facing uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Excessive speed for conditions.,c:Following other vehicles too closely.,d:All of the above.
note: Crashes often happen because drivers are distracted, driving too fast for road or weather conditions, or following other vehicles too closely. Any of these behaviors reduces your time and space to react, so all of them are common causes of collisions.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator suddenly sticks open while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition while steering to a safe area, apply brakes, and pull off the road.,b:Slam on your brakes and jump out.,c:Blow your horn continuously and stay in the lane.,d:Shift into neutral and keep steering to a safe area while braking to a stop, then turn off the ignition.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep a firm grip on the wheel, shift the transmission into neutral, and steer toward a safe place off the road. As the engine races in neutral, use steady braking to slow and stop. Once you are safely off the roadway and under control, then turn off the ignition. Never turn the key to the lock position while moving, because that can lock the steering wheel and cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:Whoever is turning has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,d:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right has the right‑of‑way and may proceed first, but only if it is clearly safe. When in doubt, communicate with eye contact or hand signals and be prepared to yield to avoid a collision.

question: When driving near large trucks, what should other drivers account for?
options: a:That large vehicles stop much sooner than cars.,b:That large vehicles can see everything behind them.,c:That trucks always yield to smaller vehicles.,d:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop. When driving near them, avoid cutting in front of them or braking suddenly, because they may not be able to stop in time. Also remember they have large blind spots along the sides and directly behind them, so give them extra space and avoid lingering where the driver cannot see you.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by easing off the gas, then brake gently.,c:Maintain current speed and keep steering locked.,d:Turn sharply toward the shoulder and brake hard.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not slam on the brakes. Instead, ease your foot off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once you have the vehicle under control and your speed has dropped, brake gently and steer to a safe place off the road before stopping completely.

question: Roads become especially slippery when:
options: a:Rain first begins for the initial 10 to 15 minutes.,b:It has been raining for several hours.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Roads are most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a light rain or drizzle. Oil and residue on the road surface mix with the water and create a slick film. After it has been raining for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction usually improves, though you should still drive carefully in wet conditions.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed immediately once the bus starts moving.,b:Watch carefully for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.
note: After a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Even after the bus starts moving, you should proceed slowly and watch carefully for children who may be walking along the road or crossing unexpectedly.

question: An 'End school zone' sign indicates:
options: a:The end of the reduced speed school zone.,b:The start of a 20 mph zone.,c:That pedestrians are more likely to be present.
note: An 'End school zone' sign tells you that the special reduced speed limit for the school zone no longer applies. After passing this sign, you may resume the regular posted speed for that roadway, as long as conditions are safe.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle.,b:Only the driver.,c:Passengers only on long trips.
note: Seat belts protect everyone in the vehicle by keeping occupants in place during a crash or sudden stop. All occupants—driver and passengers, front and rear—should wear seat belts because unbelted people can be seriously injured and can also strike or injure others in the vehicle.

question: Alcohol affects driving by:
options: a:Slowing reflexes and reaction time.,b:Waking you up and sharpening reflexes.,c:Having no effect at low doses.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and nervous system function. It reduces judgment, slows reflexes and reaction time, and makes it harder to steer, brake, and respond to hazards. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway you must:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when no vehicles or pedestrians are approaching.,b:Honk to alert others and then go.,c:Drive slowly so others will get out of your way.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road. Only proceed when the way is clear and it is safe to enter traffic.

question: During winter weather, how do overpasses and bridges compare to other roadways?
options: a:They are affected exactly the same as other roadways.,b:They thaw out before the rest of the roads.,c:They are always safer to drive on.,d:They can freeze before and remain icy longer than other road surfaces.
note: Bridges and overpasses cool down and heat up faster because air flows above and below them. In cold weather they can freeze before nearby roads and stay icy longer, even when other pavement looks just wet. Always approach them with extra caution in winter.

question: What effect does taking drugs along with alcohol have on driving risk?
options: a:No change in risk.,b:Less dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:Increases the risk of causing a crash.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both slow your reactions and judgment. When they are combined, their effects reinforce each other, making you much more impaired than with either one alone. This greatly increases your chances of causing a crash.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and continue driving.,c:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep going.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must move to the right side of the road and stop, if possible, so it has a clear path. Do not keep driving ahead of it or block intersections; stay stopped until it has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Re-enter your lane within ten feet of the passed vehicle.,b:Honk your horn repeatedly then pass.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and only re-enter the lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure the lane is clear, then signal and move into the passing lane. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, leaving a safe following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When using a roundabout, which action is required?
options: a:Yield to entering traffic.,b:Drive in a clockwise direction around the central island.,c:Stop in the center before exiting.,d:Enter from the right, yielding to traffic already in the roundabout.
note: Roundabouts in the U.S. run counterclockwise. You enter from the right side of the central island, yield to traffic already in the circle, then proceed around until your exit. Do not stop in the roundabout unless necessary to avoid a collision.

question: You must pull to the road edge and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights:
options: a:Regardless of whether it is approaching from behind or facing you.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is coming toward you from the opposite direction.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, you must pull to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of whether it is coming from behind you or toward you from the opposite direction. Stopping clears a path and reduces confusion so the emergency vehicle can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Sharply toward the curb.,b:Slightly to the right.,c:Parallel to the curb with wheels straight.,d:Sharply away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic. Always set the parking brake as well.

question: How must drivers treat pedestrians on the roadway?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian notices their vehicle.,b:Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is wrong.,c:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must use extreme care around pedestrians and do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting them. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and should yield even when they are crossing improperly, because a driver is responsible for preventing a collision whenever possible.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Before stopping, only check your blind spots.,b:Drive in the center of the lane always.,c:Brake late and hard to surprise tailgaters.,d:Avoid sudden stops and allow extra following distance.
note: To help prevent rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops and keep extra following distance so you can slow gradually. Ease off the accelerator early, signal in advance, and brake smoothly so drivers behind you have time to see what you are doing and react safely.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what is the first action you should take?
options: a:Apply firm continuous pressure to the brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Engage the parking brake.
note: On a slippery road, the first thing to do when you need to slow down is gently lift your foot off the accelerator. This lets the vehicle slow without upsetting traction. If you need to slow more, brake gently and steadily to avoid skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Stop and reverse into the correct lane.,d:Continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to turn at an intersection, you must not make sudden lane changes, cut across traffic, or back up. These actions are dangerous and illegal in many situations. Instead, continue straight, stay calm, and go to the next intersection where you can safely get into the proper lane and make your turn.

question: What single action most effectively reduces your risk of serious injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Driving at speed limits above posted values.,b:Staying in the right lane.,c:Driving only on weekdays.,d:Wearing your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash. Seat belts help keep you inside the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and work together with airbags. Other habits can improve safety, but none reduce injury risk in a crash as directly and consistently as using your seat belt every time you drive.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only marijuana.,c:Illegal drugs as well as prescription and over-the-counter medications.
note: Driving can be impaired by many types of drugs, not just illegal ones. Illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines can all affect judgment, reaction time, vision, and coordination. Always read medication labels and follow medical advice; if a drug warns against operating machinery or driving, you should not drive after taking it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,b:Make a U-turn on the interstate.,c:Continue to the next exit and exit there.,d:Stop in the lane and back up.
note: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you must never stop in a travel lane, back up, cut across traffic, or make a U‑turn. These maneuvers are extremely dangerous and usually illegal. Continue driving to the next exit, leave the interstate there, and then find a safe route back to your intended destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these must you obey over the others?
options: a:A steady red traffic light.,b:A police officer directing traffic.,c:A stop sign.
note: A police officer or other authorized person directing traffic always has priority over traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. If an officer’s hand signals or verbal directions conflict with a signal or sign, you must follow the officer’s instructions. This helps manage unusual or emergency situations safely and efficiently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,b:Only signal if other vehicles are nearby.,c:Signal only at night.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling is required by law and gives other road users time to see what you plan to do and react safely.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are yellow and placed on the left side of the road to mark the beginning of a no passing zone. They warn you that it is unsafe and illegal to pass other vehicles in that area.

question: What characteristic defines a good defensive driver?
options: a:Travels at a constant slow speed at all times.,b:Looks ahead for the actions of other drivers and anticipates hazards.,c:Relies only on other drivers to behave properly.,d:Always follows the vehicle directly in front of them closely.
note: A good defensive driver looks well ahead, watches what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists are doing, and anticipates possible hazards. This allows extra time and space to react and avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:Never under any circumstances.,b:To pass a slow vehicle when there's no oncoming traffic.,c:To turn into or out of a driveway or make a permitted left turn.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean you may not pass or drive to the left of the lines, but you may carefully cross them to make a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley when it is safe.

question: What does a green arrow signal mean?
options: a:It only applies to one-way streets.,b:Traffic may proceed and must turn in the direction of the arrow.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light is also showing.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. You must turn in that direction, and oncoming traffic and pedestrians should be stopped by a red light or "Don’t Walk" signal, though you must still check that the intersection is clear.

question: To avoid driving unsafely due to health, what should you do?
options: a:Rely on occasional rest instead of medical checks.,b:Always drive regardless of physical condition.,c:Ignore medication warnings if you feel fine.,d:Keep fit, know how medicines affect you, and drive within your limitations.
note: Staying healthy and knowing how your medical conditions and medications affect you helps you drive safely. Some medicines can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or blur your vision. You should keep physically fit, follow your doctor’s advice, read medication warnings, and avoid driving when your condition or medicine could interfere with safe driving.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:Only when pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:When changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward/away from a curb.,c:Only when turning left or right.,d:Only if your mirrors show nothing.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; the areas they miss are called blind spots. Before changing lanes, turning, or moving toward or away from a curb, you should quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check helps you see vehicles, bicycles, or motorcycles that may be in your blind spot.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you re-enter the road?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,b:Stop on the shoulder and wait for help.,c:Slow down, regain control, and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,d:Speed up and swerve back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Ease off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, and let the vehicle slow down while you regain control. When the road is clear and your speed is under control, gently steer back onto the pavement so you do not jerk the wheel and lose control.

question: A solid red arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:A driver may proceed slowly in the arrow's direction.,b:It only applies to pedestrians.,c:The same as a yellow arrow.,d:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped if you are in the lane controlled by that arrow. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or is no longer displayed. It works like a red light specifically for that turning movement.

question: When driving on slick roads, how should you handle turns?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly to avoid puddles.,c:Accelerate through the turn to maintain momentum.,d:original
note: On slick or wet roads, your tires have less grip, so it is easier to skid in a turn. Slow down before you enter the turn and steer smoothly through it. Sudden steering, braking, or acceleration in a turn on a slippery surface can cause you to lose control.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:Slow and proceed with caution in the arrow's direction.,c:Stop and then proceed when clear even if the arrow stays red.,d:Make the turn if no other traffic is present.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped in the direction of that arrow. You may not turn in that direction on a steady red arrow. You must wait until the signal changes to a green light or a green arrow before proceeding in that direction.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or vehicle operation.,b:Are always aware of the risks they're taking.,c:Drive better because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol slows your brain and body, making it harder to judge distances, react quickly, and control the vehicle. Even small amounts reduce coordination and decision‑making, so drivers who have been drinking do not have full control over themselves or their vehicle and are unsafe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, who must yield?
options: a:Drivers already on the interstate always yield.,b:The entering driver should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,c:The entering driver may force their way into traffic.,d:No one needs to yield on freeways.
note: When entering a freeway or interstate, you must use the entrance and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and then yield to vehicles already on the road. Do not force your way in; wait for a safe gap and merge smoothly without making other drivers brake hard or swerve.

question: Signs that indicate areas of public recreation are what color?
options: a:Brown.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for recreational and cultural interest areas, such as parks, campgrounds, and historic sites. When you see a brown sign, it is guiding you to or providing information about these types of locations.

question: The effect of being awake for many hours on your driving ability is similar to:
options: a:The effect of alcohol on driving ability.,b:The effect of taking amphetamines.,c:The effect of anger on driving.,d:The effect of reading before driving.
note: Being awake for a long time slows your reactions, reduces attention, and harms judgment in ways similar to alcohol. Severe fatigue can make you drift from your lane, miss hazards, or even fall asleep at the wheel, creating a level of risk comparable to driving with a significant blood alcohol concentration.

question: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Always stop no matter what.,b:Accelerate to clear the tracks quickly.,c:Prepare to yield and look both ways for trains before crossing.,d:Shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.
note: At an ungated railroad crossing without lights, you must slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be ready to stop. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming and you have enough space to clear the tracks completely without stopping on them.

question: Which of the following is illegal for passengers in a moving motor vehicle?
options: a:Using a cell phone.,b:Sleeping.,c:Having an opened alcohol container.
note: It is unlawful for anyone to possess or drink from an open alcohol container in a motor vehicle on a public road.

question: If you must drive in fog, you should:
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights only.,b:Turn on low beam headlights (not high beams).,c:Drive at the maximum posted speed.
note: In fog, you should slow down and use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Use fog lights if your vehicle has them, and adjust your speed so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Driving aggressively to control the road.,b:Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.,c:Driving against the traffic to avoid others.
note: Defensive driving means using safe driving habits to prevent crashes, such as scanning ahead, anticipating other drivers’ mistakes, adjusting to road and weather conditions, and leaving yourself space and time to react.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down firmly.,b:Firmly pump the brakes repeatedly.,c:Tap the brakes lightly.
note: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, use firm, repeated pumping of the brakes. This helps prevent the wheels from locking, so you can slow down quickly while still maintaining some steering control.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Honk your horn before changing lanes.,b:Turn your head quickly to check the blind spot before moving.,c:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,d:Assume mirrors are always enough.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see into the blind spot that mirrors cannot cover, helping you avoid collisions with vehicles you might not otherwise see.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk. As a driver, what must you do?
options: a:Speed through if you do not see pedestrians.,b:Only stop if the crosswalk is unmarked.,c:Assume pedestrians yield to vehicles.,d:Always stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk and yield the right-of-way.
note: Two solid white lines across the lane mark a crosswalk. When pedestrians are in or entering the crosswalk, you must slow or stop as necessary and yield the right-of-way to them. Never speed through or assume pedestrians must let vehicles go first.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Check mirrors and look over your shoulder to verify there is no vehicle in your blind spot.,b:Reduce your speed dramatically.,c:Sound your horn as a signal.
note: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, check your rearview and side mirrors, then glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the lane when it is clear and safe; do not rely on mirrors alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Both vehicles should wave at each other to communicate.
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps decide who goes first and prevents confusion and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:
options: a:Yield only to traffic on your left.,b:Always come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersecting roadway.
note: At a yield sign, slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection go first, entering only when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, you should:
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,b:Turn your radio up so you can hear trains better.,c:Wait for a flagger to tell you to cross.
note: At crossings with only a crossbuck and no lights or gates, you must slow, look, and listen for trains in both directions and only cross when you are sure the tracks are clear. Trains cannot stop quickly, so you must be prepared to stop and never assume the tracks are safe just because no signals are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper sequence when changing lanes?
options: a:Rely solely on your mirrors and move over.,b:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: The safe lane-change sequence is: signal first to alert others, check your mirrors to see traffic around you, then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and only then move into the lane if it is clear. Never rely only on mirrors or start moving before you signal.

question: Which actions will help you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance and ensure your headlights are working properly.,b:Drive only if you are very tired.,c:Turn off your headlights when there is oncoming traffic.,d:Use high beams at all times for the best visibility.
note: At night, visibility is reduced, so you should increase your following distance and make sure your headlights and other lights work properly. You should also avoid driving when you are tired, use low beams with oncoming traffic, and use high beams only when appropriate and when they will not blind other drivers.

question: When is it legal to cross a dashed white lane line?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:Never.,d:Only if following a motorcycle.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it when you need to change lanes, but only after checking mirrors and blind spots and making sure it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace and stay there.,c:Stay in the blind spot to prevent lane changes.
note: Driving in another driver’s blind spot is dangerous because they may not see you if they try to change lanes. Either speed up so you are clearly ahead or slow down so you are clearly behind, staying where you can be seen in their mirrors.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you proceed?
options: a:Try to squeeze between them by splitting the difference.,b:Pull onto the shoulder to pass both at once.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist when safe.
note: When you face hazards on both sides, do not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Once the lane is clear, move over to give the bicyclist at least the minimum safe passing distance required by law in your state (often 3–4 feet) and pass only when it is clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at an intersection where the light is green but heavy oncoming traffic prevents it. You should:
options: a:Wait for a safe gap in oncoming traffic before turning; you may enter the intersection to prepare if the light is green.,b:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.,c:Use the next intersection instead always.
note: You may move into the intersection to prepare for a left turn on a green light but only complete the turn when all lanes you must cross are clear.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to a:
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Yield sign.,c:Solid red light without stopping required.,d:No entry sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Higher speed always improves safety.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are an experienced driver.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.,d:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it can cause sudden braking, lane changes, and rear-end collisions. Safe driving means matching your speed to the legal limit and road, traffic, and weather conditions—not going too fast or too slow.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what is true about turning?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must proceed straight only.,c:You keep the exclusive right-of-way to turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn with the right-of-way. When it changes to a solid green light, you may still turn, but it becomes an unprotected turn. You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and turn only when there is a safe gap.

question: Which of the following helps a person overcome the influence of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Tomato juice and lime.,b:Hot coffee.,c:Fresh air.,d:Only the passage of time.
note: Only time reduces a person’s blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, fresh air, cold showers, or other “remedies” may make someone feel more awake but do not make them less impaired or safe to drive. The body must metabolize the alcohol over time.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop immediately in your lane.,b:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.,c:Proceed slowly and allow it to pass on your left.
note: On a two-lane or undivided road, you must yield to emergency vehicles with lights and siren by pulling as far to the right as is safe and stopping. This creates a clear path in the center of the road so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: Which restraints are most effective in a crash?
options: a:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag used together.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Only a lap belt.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both the lap/shoulder belt and the airbag together. The seat belt keeps you properly positioned and prevents ejection, while the airbag provides extra cushioning. Airbags alone are not enough without a seat belt.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, after one train passes you should:
options: a:Look for another train on the other track before crossing.,b:Always stop and call authorities.,c:Assume it is safe to proceed immediately.
note: At crossings with more than one track, a second train can approach from either direction after the first one passes. Always wait until you have a clear view of all tracks and are sure no other train is coming before you start across.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:
options: a:You can see far enough ahead to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:You are able to clearly see the road ahead only a short distance.,c:Your vehicle is the fastest on the road.
note: You may only pass on a two-way, two-lane road when you can clearly see far enough ahead to complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. If your view is limited by hills, curves, weather, or other vehicles, you must not pass.

question: When a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon shows two flashing red lights, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding with caution.,b:Slow and proceed if clear.,c:Ignore it unless pedestrians are visible.
note: When a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon shows two flashing red lights, you must first come to a complete stop. After stopping, you may proceed only if the crosswalk is clear of pedestrians and it is safe to go. Treat it like a stop sign: stop fully, then proceed with caution when the way is clear.

question: If you approach railroad crossing with signals flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and look for a train, at least 15 feet from the nearest rail.,b:Slow down and proceed if you do not see a train.,c:Speed up to beat the train.
note: Flashing signals at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop before the tracks, no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail, and wait until the lights stop flashing and it is clearly safe to cross. Never try to beat the train or go around lowered gates.

question: What are the colors of highway guide signs that show distances to exits and destinations?
options: a:Black background with white letters.,b:Yellow background with black letters.,c:Red background with white letters.,d:Green background with white letters.
note: Highway guide signs that show exits, directions, and distances to destinations are green with white letters or symbols. These signs help you navigate to cities, streets, and highway routes.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that what will soon follow?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady green light.,c:A steady red light.
note: A steady yellow traffic signal means the light is about to turn steady red. You should stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, proceed carefully through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a “Reduced speed, 35 mph” sign mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,b:The new speed begins at the next sign.,c:You have plenty of time to slow down after passing the sign.,d:The reduction is only a suggestion.
note: A “Reduced speed, 35 mph” sign means the new 35 mph speed limit starts at that sign. You must already be at or slowing to that speed as you reach the sign and obey that limit from that point onward, unless another sign changes it.

question: When you encounter a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the pedestrian and proceed.,b:Assume they will avoid your vehicle.,c:Take the right-of-way and proceed.,d:Slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, yield the right‑of‑way, and be prepared to stop. Do not honk, rush past, or assume they will avoid you. Give them extra time and space to cross safely.

question: At a railroad crossing where you do not see or hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:Only during nighttime hours.,b:Only when a train is visible.,c:If you are towing a trailer only.,d:If a stop sign is posted or if crossing lights are flashing or a gate is lowered.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a stop sign is posted, the red lights are flashing, the gate is lowered, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is close enough to be a hazard. Never proceed just because you don’t see or hear a train; always obey the signs, signals, and gates.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:A pedestrian lane.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,d:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A solid white line is used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. It indicates that lane changes are discouraged or sometimes prohibited. A center line between traffic moving in opposite directions is yellow, not white.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane road, when you see a 'Merging traffic' sign you should:
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by moving over if safe and possible.,b:Always keep your current speed and position.,c:Honk at incoming drivers to warn them off.
note: When you see a merging traffic sign on a multi‑lane road, you should help create a smooth, safe merge. If possible and safe, move over to give entering vehicles space, or adjust your speed so they can merge safely. Do not maintain speed and position in a way that blocks them, and do not use your horn to intimidate other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopped in a line and the vehicles ahead move through a stop sign. If no cross traffic is present, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before moving on.,c:Slowly roll through the stop sign to maintain traffic flow.,d:Honk to warn pedestrians before moving.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, even if vehicles ahead have already stopped and gone. You cannot rely on the car in front of you; you must make your own full stop and then proceed when it is safe.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver who is following you too closely?
options: a:Speed up to increase the gap between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to make them fall back.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass.
note: If someone is following too closely, create a safe situation for yourself by increasing the space in front of your vehicle. When it is safe, change lanes to let them pass, or gradually slow down to encourage them to go around you. Never slam on your brakes, because that can cause a rear-end collision.

question: For drivers age 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of:
options: a:0.08 percent or higher.,b:0.05 percent or higher.,c:0.02 percent or higher.
note: In most U.S. jurisdictions, for drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. However, you can still be arrested for DUI at lower levels if your driving is impaired, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking at all.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents:
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The suggested safe speed under all conditions.,c:The speed you must always travel regardless of conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit when conditions are less than ideal, such as in bad weather, heavy traffic, or poor visibility. Some areas also post special minimum speed limits to keep traffic flowing safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When do you have the right-of-way while turning left at a signal?
options: a:When facing a solid green light.,b:When facing a flashing yellow light.,c:When facing a green arrow pointing left.,d:When oncoming traffic is turning right.
note: A steady green left arrow gives you a protected left turn. Oncoming traffic, bicycles, and pedestrians facing the opposite signal are stopped, so you have the right-of-way to complete your turn. With a solid green or flashing yellow, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: To prepare for anything ahead on the road, you should:
options: a:Continually scan the entire roadway and roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at the center of the road only.,c:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake.,d:Focus only on the vehicle directly ahead of you.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and behind them. By looking well ahead and checking mirrors and roadsides, you can spot hazards early and have more time to react smoothly and safely, instead of making sudden, risky maneuvers.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:Only to the left and right.,c:On all sides of the vehicle.,d:Only behind the vehicle.
note: Keeping a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle gives you room to brake, change lanes, or steer away from hazards. Space in front, behind, and to both sides reduces the chance of collisions and gives you more time to react.

question: When a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon shows two solid red lights, what must drivers do?
options: a:Proceed with caution without stopping.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped for pedestrians.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon displaying two steady red lights requires drivers to stop and remain stopped for pedestrians crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you prepare to make a left turn, what should you be doing?
options: a:Signal in advance, slow gradually, and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Speed up to beat oncoming traffic.,c:Make the turn from the far right lane.,d:Ignore pedestrians if you have a green light.
note: Before a left turn, signal well in advance, slow smoothly, and move into the proper lane. Scan for oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk, and yield to them before turning when it is safe.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, what actions should you take?
options: a:Drive cautiously, reduce speed, and use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beam headlights to better see ahead.,c:Drive at normal speed if traffic is light.,d:Turn off all lights to reduce glare.
note: In fog, slow down, increase following distance, and use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see, while low beams and fog lights (if equipped) help you see the road and be seen by others.

question: If another vehicle is about to collide with you, you should:
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Do nothing and hope they avoid you.,c:Sound your horn to warn the other driver and pedestrians.,d:Sound your horn and be prepared to brake or steer to reduce the impact.
note: If a collision seems likely, use your horn to warn the other driver and pedestrians, and at the same time be ready to brake or steer to reduce the impact or avoid the crash. Your horn is a safety device meant to alert others to immediate danger, not to express anger.

question: If an aggressive driver is following you closely and acting hostile, what should you do?
options: a:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Try to get out of their way and avoid confrontation.,d:Speed up to challenge them.
note: If another driver is aggressive or tailgating, do not respond or try to punish them. Stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and safely move out of their way when possible. If you feel threatened, pull over in a safe, public place and contact law enforcement.

question: When should you reduce your speed when approaching a curve in the road?
options: a:Only if you feel uncomfortable.,b:After you have entered the curve.,c:Before you enter the curve.,d:Only if another car is behind you.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve so your vehicle is at a safe speed as you begin turning. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially in poor road or weather conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Just before you begin to change lanes to pass.,b:Only if the vehicle ahead signals.,c:After you have already started the pass.,d:Signal early enough that other drivers understand your intention.
note: Always signal well in advance before changing lanes or passing so other drivers clearly understand what you plan to do. The signal must be on before you start moving into the other lane and should give nearby drivers enough time to see and react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe to make a U-turn?
options: a:At the crest of a hill or near a curve because visibility is limited.,b:In the middle of an intersection if traffic is clear.,c:Anywhere drivers can see you for at least 500 feet in both directions.,d:On a divided highway where openings are provided for U-turns.
note: Never make a U-turn where other drivers cannot see you well, such as at the top of a hill, on or near a curve, or where signs prohibit U-turns. In many states, you must be visible to other traffic for at least 500 feet in both directions before making a U-turn.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Warning of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:Alerts drivers to school zones.,c:Indicates recreational areas.,d:Shows route information.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They are usually yellow or orange and alert you to existing or possible hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or work zones.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beams).,b:Use only your parking lights while driving.,c:Do not turn on any lights.
note: At dusk, dawn, or on overcast days, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights so other drivers can see you more easily. Parking lights alone are not sufficient and are not a substitute for headlights while driving. Use low beams whenever visibility is reduced, and dim them for oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle closely.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels run off the pavement, what is the correct action?
options: a:Accelerate and turn sharply back onto the road.,b:Ease off the accelerator, steer parallel to the roadway, slow down, then carefully steer back on when safe.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm and avoid jerking the steering wheel. Ease off the accelerator, keep steering straight and parallel to the roadway, and slow down gradually. Once the vehicle is under control and there is a safe gap in traffic, gently steer back onto the pavement. Sudden acceleration or sharp turns can cause you to lose control or skid.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is true?
options: a:There is no need to change driving style in rain or fog.,b:You should ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.,c:A sudden change in weather requires you to adjust your driving.
note: When weather changes suddenly—such as rain, fog, snow, or strong wind—you must adjust how you drive. Reduce speed, increase following distance, and use appropriate lights so you can see and be seen. You should pay attention to all traffic around you, including vehicles behind you, because stopping distances and visibility are reduced.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,b:Move as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.,c:Creep into the intersection to get a better view.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through without stopping and blocking cross traffic. If vehicles ahead are stopped and the intersection is blocked, wait behind the stop line or crosswalk until there is enough space for your vehicle to clear the intersection completely.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around a lowered gate.,b:Drive faster to beat an approaching train.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,d:Ignore it if no signals are present.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching train tracks. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is nearby or signals are activated. Never try to drive around lowered gates or speed up to beat a train; trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way.

question: What driving behavior can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly from a stop.,b:Sitting idling in your driveway.,c:Slowing down and coasting to avoid unnecessary stops.,d:Frequent hard braking to control speed.
note: Slowing down early and coasting toward stops reduces the need for hard braking and rapid acceleration, both of which waste fuel. Smooth, gradual speed changes and anticipating traffic flow are key habits for conserving gasoline.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines painted across lanes) located?
options: a:In curves and on hills only.,b:Only on one-way streets.,c:Next to churches and schools only.,d:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines across the lane that show exactly where you must stop at an intersection or before a crosswalk. You must stop with the front of your vehicle behind this line when required by a stop sign, red light, or other control.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, you should glance:
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:Only at the rearview mirror.,c:At your side mirror.,d:Over your left shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward to see the blind spot. For a left lane change, look over your left shoulder to be sure no vehicle is hidden beside you.

question: What does an orange-colored traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A hospital zone ahead.,b:A railroad crossing ahead.,c:A school zone ahead.,d:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work or incident areas. They warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead so you can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

question: When is it permissible to cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:To pass slower traffic at any time.,b:Only when making a left turn into a driveway or side street.,c:During daytime hours only.,d:Whenever the lane beside you is clear.
note: A solid yellow center line means you must not cross it to pass other vehicles. You may cross a solid yellow only when making a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or side street, and only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns indicates:
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,c:You should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction without yielding.
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may proceed with the turn, but only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. It is a permissive signal, not a stop signal, so you move when it is safe and clear.

question: If a vehicle with ABS begins to lose traction on a slippery road, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the accelerator.
note: With ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it while steering where you want to go. The system rapidly pumps the brakes for you, helping maintain steering control. Do not pump the brakes yourself, and never accelerate when you are losing traction.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:The area directly behind your vehicle.,b:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,c:The area visible in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that are not visible in your mirrors. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: What risks do worn or bald tires pose?
options: a:They can increase your stopping distance.,b:They improve fuel efficiency.,c:They make steering more precise.,d:They reduce the chance of hydroplaning.
note: Worn or bald tires have less tread, which reduces grip on the road. This increases your stopping distance, makes steering and cornering less stable, and greatly raises the risk of skidding or hydroplaning on wet roads.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:The full width of a lane, the same as other vehicles.,b:Only the bicycle lane.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use the full width of a traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Drivers should not crowd them or share the lane side‑by‑side unless the law specifically allows lane sharing between motorcycles.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Yield to the transit vehicle to allow it to re-enter safely.,b:Honk to warn the driver.,c:Speed up and pass the bus.
note: When a transit bus signals that it is pulling out from a stop, you should be prepared to yield so it can re-enter traffic safely. This may mean slowing, changing lanes, or stopping if needed. Giving buses space helps protect passengers and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: What do your vehicle's brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:You are about to make a turn.,b:You are changing lanes.,c:You are slowing down or stopping.,d:Your parking brake is engaged.
note: Brake lights turn on when you press the brake pedal and tell drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This advance warning gives them time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions. Make sure your brake lights work properly at all times.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Overcorrect and turn the wheel hard away from the skid.,b:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: In a skid, you should stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction the rear of your vehicle is sliding. This is often described as steering in the direction of the skid. Once the vehicle begins to straighten out, you can gently correct your steering to stay in your lane.

question: Green pavement markings typically indicate:
options: a:Emergency-only lanes.,b:HOV lanes exclusively.,c:Areas with potential conflicts between bicycles and motor vehicles.
note: Green pavement markings are used to highlight areas where bicycles and motor vehicles may cross paths, such as at conflict zones in bike lanes or intersections. When you see green pavement, slow down, check carefully for bicyclists, and be prepared to yield when required.

question: You see the driver ahead driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space because the driver may be inattentive.,b:Follow their example.,c:Speed up to pass immediately.
note: A driver who is talking, gesturing, or driving with one hand may be distracted and slower to react. Increase your following distance so you have more time and space to respond if that driver makes a sudden or unsafe move.

question: How far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph need to stop?
options: a:About 50 feet.,b:About 125 feet.,c:Up to 400 feet.
note: A fully loaded tractor‑trailer needs much more distance to stop than a passenger car. At 55 mph, a large truck can require close to 400 feet to come to a complete stop because of its weight and longer braking distance. This is why you should never cut closely in front of a truck or brake suddenly when a truck is following you.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Keep looking straight into the oncoming headlights.,c:Look over your shoulder.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you if you look directly at them. To reduce glare, shift your eyes slightly to the right edge of your lane and use the right side of the road or the white edge line as a guide.
