This helps you maintain your lane position while protecting your night vision.

question: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Improved coordination.,c:Faster judgment.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and body functions. Even small amounts reduce concentration, slow reaction time, and impair judgment and coordination. It never improves coordination or speeds up judgment, which is why any drinking can make driving unsafe.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag.,b:An airbag is harmless to infants and small children.,c:Children age 12 and under should always ride in the front seat.,d:Seat belts are optional for backseat passengers.
note: Airbags are designed for adults and can seriously injure or kill infants in rear‑facing seats if they deploy. A rear‑facing infant seat must never be placed in front of an active passenger airbag. Children are safest properly restrained in the back seat, using the correct child safety seat or booster for their age, height, and weight.

question: When following a motorcycle, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Four seconds.,d:One second.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles and offer less protection to the rider. To give yourself enough time to react if a motorcycle stops or falls suddenly, you should follow at least four seconds behind. This larger space cushion improves safety for both you and the rider.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center two-way left-turn lane, what maneuvers are permitted?
options: a:You may make left turns from either direction.,b:You may use it for passing slow traffic.,c:You may drive through it as a through lane.,d:You may make U-turns from it only where signs or local law specifically allow.
note: A center two‑way left‑turn lane is only for making left turns from either direction and, where specifically allowed by local law and signs, for carefully beginning or completing a turn. It must not be used for passing, for driving as a through lane, or for making U‑turns unless signs clearly permit U‑turns from that lane.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,d:Only dangerous for inexperienced drivers.
note: Driving after drinking any amount of alcohol is a serious traffic safety problem. Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and affects judgment, so even a small amount can make driving unsafe for any driver, experienced or not.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed of your vehicle.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance increases with higher speed and is also affected by the condition of your brakes and tires and by the road surface. Wet, icy, or gravel roads and worn brakes or tires all increase the distance it takes your vehicle to stop.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching from any direction, what action is required?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane.,b:Keep driving but do not block intersections.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop until it has passed.,d:Immediately back up to clear the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right side of the road and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed or an officer directs you to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions make driving less than perfect, such as rain or poor visibility.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:Only when entering a highway with other cars.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit whenever rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, poor road surfaces, or limited visibility make the posted speed unsafe.

question: A stop sign has what shape?
options: a:Octagon.,b:Circle.,c:Rectangle.
note: Stop signs are the only standard road signs that are octagonal (eight-sided). When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection.

question: When it starts to rain while you're driving, you should:
options: a:Slow down, turn on headlights, and if visibility is poor pull off safely.,b:Increase speed to get home faster.,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed limit.
note: When rain begins, the road can be especially slippery from oil and debris. You should slow down, turn on your headlights so others can see you, and if visibility or traction becomes poor, pull off the road safely and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Only when a police officer is present.,b:At an intersection with a stop sign, at a red light, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,c:Only when other vehicles are present.,d:Never unless there is an emergency.
note: You must stop at stop signs, at red traffic lights (unless a legal turn on red is allowed and safe), and whenever a police officer or other authorized traffic officer directs you to stop. Failing to stop in these situations is a traffic violation and can cause crashes.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,b:You won't be able to see their turn signals.,c:It makes traffic flow slower.
note: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or distance to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you room to brake smoothly and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: Fluorescent yellow-green road signs are used to warn drivers about which situation?
options: a:Hospital locations.,b:Speed limits.,c:School zones and pedestrian or bicycle warnings.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Fluorescent yellow-green signs are used for school zones, school crossings, and pedestrian or bicycle warning signs. When you see this color, be prepared to slow down and watch carefully for people walking or biking, especially children.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, you should:
options: a:Shift into park immediately.,b:Reach down and try to pull up the pedal while continuing to steer.,c:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake, then pull off safely and turn off the engine.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep control of the vehicle by shifting to neutral so the engine is no longer driving the wheels. Apply steady, firm brake pressure, steer to the side of the road, and once you are safely off the roadway, turn off the engine. Do not shift into park while moving, as this can damage the transmission and may cause loss of control.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A circular green sign.,d:A reflective orange triangle (slow-moving vehicle emblem).
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border. It is mounted on the rear of vehicles that cannot travel faster than about 25 mph, such as farm equipment or some construction vehicles, to warn faster traffic to use extra caution and be prepared to slow down.

question: If a driver is turning while a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield.,b:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.,d:The driver may proceed if turning quickly.
note: When turning, drivers must yield to pedestrians who are legally crossing the street, including at intersections and marked or unmarked crosswalks, even when there is no traffic signal. The driver must wait until the pedestrian has safely cleared the path before completing the turn.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:
options: a:Your body weight.,b:The type or name of the alcoholic beverage (what matters is total alcohol consumed, not the drink label).,c:How much time passes between drinks.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is determined mainly by how much alcohol you consume, your body weight, how quickly you drink, and how much time your body has to eliminate alcohol. The type of alcoholic beverage matters only because different drinks contain different amounts of alcohol per serving; what truly affects BAC is the total amount of alcohol taken in, not whether it came from beer, wine, or liquor.

question: Compared to daytime driving, nighttime driving is generally:
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Nighttime driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far or as clearly, making it harder to detect hazards in time. Headlight glare, reduced depth perception, and the increased likelihood of drowsy or impaired drivers on the road all raise the risk of crashes after dark.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:The center of the road.,b:The left side of the road.,c:The right side of the road.,d:Directly at the headlights.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, you should avoid looking directly at the bright lights because they can temporarily blind you. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road to use it as a guide while keeping your vehicle centered and safely in your lane.

question: Tailgating is:
options: a:Following another vehicle too closely so you do not have enough space to stop safely.,b:Only an inconvenience.,c:The fastest way to reach your destination.
note: Never tailgate; it is illegal in many places and greatly increases rear-end collision risk.

question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, drivers should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop every time.,c:Increase speed to get through quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards. You do not have to stop unless it is necessary for safety, but you must be prepared to yield if needed.

question: Which type of sign warns you about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs are usually yellow with black symbols or words and alert you to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or merging traffic. They give you time to slow down or adjust your driving to stay safe.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions.,b:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe.,c:Drivers may not pass.,d:A pedestrian crossing.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: If your wheels run off the edge of the pavement, what is the safest way to return to the road?
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to quickly slam back onto the pavement.,b:Increase speed and abruptly steer back onto the road.,c:Gently brake, slow down, and steer gradually back onto the pavement when safe.,d:Slam on the brakes and stop in the shoulder.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the gas, and avoid sudden steering or hard braking. Slow down gradually while staying on the shoulder, then when your speed is under control and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement at a shallow angle.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, you should:
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus before driving.,b:Drive quickly to get the trip over with.,c:Be fine to drive—emotions don't affect driving.
note: Strong emotions like anger, fear, or crying can narrow your attention and slow your reactions, making you more likely to make mistakes. It is safest to wait until you have calmed down and can fully focus on driving before you start or continue your trip.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Merging traffic only.,c:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,d:Come to a full stop before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means the intersection is not protected by a full stop signal. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down, scan carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When conditions reduce visibility or make it harder to stop, such as behind a large vehicle, in bad weather, or in heavy traffic.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when following a motorcycle in good weather.
note: You should leave extra space whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop in time. This includes following large vehicles that block your view, driving in bad weather, heavy traffic, at higher speeds, or when following motorcycles, bicycles, or other vulnerable road users. More distance gives you time to react if they brake or swerve suddenly.

question: Which action helps prevent crashes by communicating with other road users?
options: a:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your vehicle.,b:Drive only on side streets to avoid interactions.,c:Use your signals and horn when appropriate.
note: Other drivers can respond safely only if they know what you plan to do. Using your turn signals, brake lights, and horn when needed lets others anticipate your lane changes, turns, and stops, which helps prevent sudden conflicts and crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When you are in a school zone.,b:If it requires driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.,d:If the vehicle ahead is waiting to make a left turn and there is a sufficient lane on the right.
note: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn and there is a clearly marked lane or enough paved roadway to do so safely without leaving the pavement. You must never drive off the paved portion of the road or use the shoulder to pass.

question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow plus a red light means:
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.,b:You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.,c:You may only drive straight ahead.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow; oncoming traffic and cross traffic are stopped by a red light. The red light applies to all other movements, so you may only move in the direction of the green arrow when it is safe.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles on the road?
options: a:Motorcycles always stop more quickly than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers.,c:Motorcyclists rarely use helmets.,d:Motorcycles are more difficult to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and narrower than cars, so they are easier to overlook in mirrors and blind spots. Their size also makes it harder to judge how fast they are approaching, so you must look carefully and allow extra space when sharing the road with them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane furthest from your original lane.,b:Into the lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Any lane that appears clear.,d:The center lane regardless of markings.
note: When turning left onto a one‑way street, you should turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you turned from, unless lane markings or signs direct you otherwise. This keeps traffic organized and reduces the chance of sideswipe or head‑on collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where must your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Near the left side of the street.,c:As close as possible to the right side of the street.
note: For a right turn, you should approach and complete the turn from as close to the right curb or edge of the roadway as is practical. Staying to the right helps you turn safely and predictably and prevents you from cutting across other lanes.

question: What is the best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly maintained and reduce speed when roads are wet.,b:Use cruise control on wet roads.,c:Drive faster to get through puddles quickly.,d:Inflate tires to the maximum pressure regardless of conditions.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce the chance of hydroplaning, keep your tires properly inflated and with good tread, and slow down whenever the road is wet. Avoid sudden steering or braking and do not use cruise control in heavy rain.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Never; you have the right-of-way.,b:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,c:Only when other vehicles yield first.
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing lights. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer or traffic control.

question: When a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, the driver is indicating:
options: a:An intention to stop or slow.,b:An intention to turn left.,c:An intention to turn right.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn. A left arm bent upward means a right turn. A left arm extended downward with the palm to the rear means you intend to stop or slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to which road users?
options: a:Vehicles already in the roundabout, bicyclists, and pedestrians.,b:Only pedestrians.,c:Only vehicles entering from the left.,d:Only emergency vehicles.
note: Before entering a roundabout, slow down and yield to traffic already in the circle, including vehicles and bicyclists, and yield to pedestrians in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Enter only when there is a safe gap and proceed in a counterclockwise direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb is:
options: a:A good driving habit and required by law.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Required during the maneuver but not before it.,d:Only necessary during daylight hours.
note: Turn signals communicate your intentions so others can react safely. The law requires you to signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb—typically for at least the last 100 feet before the maneuver (more at higher speeds where required). Always signal, even if you think no one else is around.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
options: a:They are blind and may not see or hear your vehicle.,b:They are always accompanied by a guide dog that obeys traffic.,c:They must yield to vehicles.,d:They cannot enter crosswalks.
note: A white cane indicates the pedestrian is blind or visually impaired. They may not see your vehicle and may also have limited ability to judge its speed or direction. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and always yield the right-of-way to protect them.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The alcohol cancels the drug's effects.,b:There will never be any interaction.,c:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,d:The combination is always safe.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs often makes both substances more powerful and unpredictable. This can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment, making driving extremely dangerous.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without signals, what should you do?
options: a:Always bring your vehicle to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop after checking both directions for trains.,c:Assume all railroad crossings have signals and proceed normally.
note: At a railroad crossing without signals, slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be ready to stop. Only proceed when you are sure no train is coming. Never assume crossings will have lights or gates to warn you.

question: What is the only reliable way to lower your BAC?
options: a:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up.,c:Exercise to speed up alcohol metabolism.
note: Your body needs time to process and eliminate alcohol. Coffee, exercise, cold showers, or other tricks do not speed up this process or lower your BAC. Only waiting long enough will reduce your blood alcohol concentration.

question: When stopped in line of traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and can proceed without checking.,b:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,c:There is enough space ahead so your vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping.
note: Before you drive onto railroad tracks, make sure there is enough space on the far side so your entire vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping. Never stop on the tracks or try to pass other vehicles while crossing.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.,b:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.,c:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and drive to a safe area before stopping.,d:Steer sharply to the side and stop immediately in the lane.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer, but it will require much more physical effort, especially at low speeds. Grip the wheel firmly, slow down gradually, and use extra effort to steer the vehicle to the side of the road or another safe location. Once safely out of traffic, stop and get the problem checked before driving again.

question: How should you treat traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:You must follow them only when other traffic is present.,b:They are merely suggestions.,c:They only apply to commercial vehicles.,d:They must always be obeyed.
note: Traffic control devices—signs, signals, and pavement markings—are legal requirements, not suggestions. They are designed to regulate, warn, and guide traffic to keep everyone safe. You must obey them at all times unless a police officer or other authorized person is directing you to do something different.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They obey different traffic laws.,c:They always have the legal right-of-way.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and less visible than cars and trucks, and they can appear suddenly in your path. Because they are more vulnerable in a crash, drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and anticipate that these road users may be harder to see and may move unpredictably.

question: If you are upset or angry before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the radio loud to forget about it.,b:Drive fast on the highway to release tension.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
note: Strong emotions like anger, stress, or sadness can distract you, slow your reaction time, and lead to aggressive or risky driving decisions. If you are upset, wait until you have calmed down before driving so you can focus fully on the road and make safe, rational choices.

question: What is the consequence of refusing an alcohol analysis test when suspected of OUI in Massachusetts?
options: a:There are no consequences for refusal.,b:You get a warning only.,c:Refusal is recommended.,d:Your driver's license will be suspended.
note: Under Massachusetts’ implied consent law, by driving you agree to take a chemical test if lawfully arrested for OUI. If you refuse the test, the RMV will suspend your driver’s license or right to operate for a set period, separate from any criminal penalties for OUI. This suspension happens even if you are later found not guilty of the OUI charge.

question: In rainy driving conditions which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and on the road, creating glare that makes it harder for you to see and can blind other drivers. Low beams give better visibility in poor weather while reducing glare.

question: Which of these is important when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Signal your intentions in advance.,b:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before moving.,d:All of the above.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move when you are sure the lane is clear and you have enough space. Doing all three steps helps prevent collisions with vehicles you may not see in your mirrors alone.

question: Being distracted while driving:
options: a:Usually causes drivers to drive faster.,b:Usually causes slower reactions to hazards.,c:Is not dangerous.
note: Distractions such as using a phone, eating, or adjusting controls take your attention away from the road and slow your reaction time. When you are distracted, you may not notice hazards as quickly, which increases your risk of a crash even if your speed does not change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your steering wheel?
options: a:Signal and keep the wheels turned left.,b:Signal and keep the wheels straight while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you turn.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your front wheels pointed straight. If another vehicle hits you from behind while your wheels are turned left, your car can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight helps you go forward instead of into opposing lanes if you are struck.

question: When is it illegal to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When crossing would interfere with other traffic.,b:When turning left into a private driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.
note: A single broken line means you may cross it to pass or change lanes only when it is safe. It is illegal and unsafe to cross if doing so would interfere with other traffic, such as forcing another driver to slow or swerve. Always check that you have enough space and visibility before crossing.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Just set the parking brake.,c:Leave the engine running if it's cold out.
note: When leaving an unattended vehicle you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in school zones?
options: a:There is no single standard; obey the posted school‑zone speed limit.,b:20 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: School‑zone speed limits are set by each state or locality and vary widely (often 15–25 mph, sometimes higher), and they usually apply only at certain times or when children are present. Because there is no single standard speed for all U.S. school zones, you must always obey the posted school‑zone speed limit signs rather than assuming a default number.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what is required?
options: a:Slow down until it passes.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren or flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.,d:It only affects judgment at very high doses.
note: Alcohol slows your reactions, reduces coordination, blurs vision, and weakens your ability to judge speed, distance, and risk. Because it harms both your driving skills and your judgment, any amount of alcohol can make driving unsafe, even if you feel fine.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching using siren and/or lights, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and slow down but stay in your lane.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving.,c:Pull to the right and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or siren, you must immediately yield by moving to the right edge or curb of the road and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic. This creates a clear lane so responders can reach emergencies quickly and safely.

question: Where is it unlawful to park?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:Anywhere on a hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: Parking on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane is illegal because it blocks pedestrians and cyclists who have the right of way in those areas. Always park parallel and within the required distance from the curb (often 12–18 inches, depending on state law) and never stop or park where you obstruct designated walking or biking space.

question: What may reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Ignoring posted speed limits.,b:Speeding to get ahead of other drivers.,c:Allowing extra travel time and using proper signals.,d:Yelling at drivers who cut you off.
note: Allowing extra travel time, obeying speed limits, and using turn signals early and clearly helps you stay calm and predictable, which reduces the chances of conflicts with other drivers. Aggressive behaviors like speeding, tailgating, or yelling at others increase tension and the risk of road rage incidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To make a left turn from a multilane, one-way street onto another one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The nearest bicycle lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.,d:The left lane.
note: When turning left from a multilane, one‑way street onto another one‑way street, you must start from the left lane because it is the lane closest to the center and is designated for left turns. Complete the turn into the left lane of the street you are entering, then change lanes if needed when it is safe and legal.

question: How should a lap belt be positioned for proper restraint?
options: a:Loose across the stomach.,b:Snugly across your hip bones and low on the pelvis.,c:Hidden beneath the seat cushion.,d:Across your neck for support.
note: A lap belt should fit snugly across the hip bones and low on the pelvis, not across the stomach. The strong bones of the hips can better withstand crash forces, while a belt across the abdomen can cause serious internal injuries in a collision. The belt should be tight and low, lying across the upper thighs and hip area.

question: If you drive through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to do what?
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Potentially run out into the street without looking.
note: In areas where children are playing, you must anticipate that they may suddenly run into the street without looking or understanding traffic dangers. Slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop quickly. Extra caution is needed near schools, parks, residential areas, and anywhere children are present.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, you should allow a larger space cushion because:
options: a:There is more oncoming traffic uphill.,b:It is easier to stop on an incline.,c:The vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic starts moving again.
note: When you are stopped facing uphill, a vehicle with a manual or automatic transmission can roll backward slightly when the driver moves from the brake to the accelerator. Leaving extra space in front of you creates a safety cushion so that if the vehicle ahead rolls back, it will not strike your car.

question: After a collision, which action should drivers take at or near the scene?
options: a:Drive away if no one appears injured.,b:Stand or walk in traffic lanes to inspect damage.,c:Stop the vehicle at or near the scene.,d:Leave the ignitions of wrecked vehicles on.
note: After any collision, you are legally required to stop at or as close as safely possible to the scene. Do not drive away, do not stand in live traffic lanes, and turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles if you can safely do so to reduce fire risk. Move vehicles out of traffic if they are drivable and it is safe.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by what color lines?
options: a:White lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Red lines.
note: In the United States, white lane lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Red lines are not used to separate normal travel lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on a highway outside thickly settled areas and business districts is:
options: a:Varies by state; follow your state’s default rural highway limit and posted signs.,b:50 mph in all states.,c:10 mph.
note: Speed limits that apply when no sign is posted are called statutory or default limits, and they vary by state. Many states use 55 mph or higher as the default limit on rural highways outside business or thickly settled areas, while others use 50 mph. Always follow the posted limit; if no sign is present, follow your state’s specific default limit and slow down further when weather, traffic, or road conditions require.

question: If another driver behaves aggressively toward you, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Get out of your vehicle to confront them.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.,d:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: If another driver is aggressive, your goal is to avoid escalating the situation. Do not retaliate, make gestures, or confront them. Instead, stay calm, avoid eye contact, slow slightly if needed, and allow them to pass so you can increase the distance between your vehicles.

question: When following a heavy truck uphill, you should know:
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed and you may not be able to pass safely on a hill.,b:The truck will always keep the posted speed limit.,c:It is always legal to pass on a hill if you have room.
note: When following a heavy truck uphill, expect it to slow below the posted speed limit because large vehicles lose speed on grades. Passing on a hill is often unsafe or illegal due to limited visibility and solid yellow center lines, so you may not be able to pass safely even if the truck is going slowly.

question: When a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon shows a solid yellow light, you must:
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Come to a complete stop immediately.,c:Proceed without change.
note: On a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon, a solid yellow light means the beacon is about to change to red. You must slow down and be prepared to stop for pedestrians, just as you would for a solid yellow traffic signal that is changing to red.

question: Bicycles on the road are considered:
options: a:Vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,b:Obstructions that must always yield to cars.,c:Non-traffic objects.
note: Bicycles on the road are treated as vehicles. Cyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles, including obeying traffic signals and signs. Drivers must yield, pass, and share the road with bicycles as they would with other vehicles, while also giving them extra space for safety.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed only if the bus driver waves you on.,b:Pass slowly if you think children are clear.,c:Honk before passing on the left.,d:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, all traffic in both directions (in most situations) must stop until children are safe and the arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the left has the right-of-way at all times.,d:The largest vehicle has right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, the driver who arrives and stops first has the right-of-way and goes first. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. If there is any confusion, drivers should communicate with eye contact and proceed cautiously.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn others in hazardous situations, such as a child about to run into the street.,b:To greet a friend at an intersection.,c:While passing a bicyclist.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision or warn others of a hazard, such as a child about to run into the street or a driver who is about to hit you. Do not use the horn to greet people, express anger, or for non‑emergency reasons.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only use the outside mirrors.
note: Mirrors alone cannot show areas directly beside and slightly behind your vehicle. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, then quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign at an intersection, how should you check traffic before proceeding?
options: a:Look only forward and go when clear.,b:Look left first, then right, then left again.,c:Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.,d:Check your rearview mirror then go.
note: At a stop sign, scan carefully in all directions. Look left first (where traffic comes from first), then right, then left again before moving. Also check straight ahead and, when relevant, behind you to be sure the intersection is clear and safe before proceeding.

question: Your chances of being in a collision start to rise after consuming how many alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Only after four or more drinks.,b:After three or more drinks only.,c:Even after one drink your crash risk is higher.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Crash risk begins to increase even after one drink, so the only truly safe choice for driving is to avoid drinking altogether before you drive.

question: While driving on a divided multilane highway you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are free.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Slow down, move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop when safe.,d:Speed up to clear the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely slow down, move to the right side of the road to create a clear path, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat so you can see and reach controls properly.,b:Your rearview mirror only.,c:Your steering wheel only.
note: Adjusting your seat first ensures you can reach the pedals, steering wheel, and other controls comfortably and maintain a clear view of the road and mirrors. Once seated correctly, you then adjust mirrors and steering wheel position as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should you do?
options: a:You have the right-of-way.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:Force your way into traffic if necessary.,d:Stop only if traffic is heavy.
note: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the roadway, including vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians. Enter only when there is a safe gap so you do not force other road users to slow or change lanes suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it unsafe or unlawful to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a hill or curve, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only when a police officer is present.,c:When the vehicle ahead is traveling below the speed limit.,d:When the passing lane is empty.
note: Passing is unsafe and often illegal where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic or where conflicts are likely, such as on hills or curves, at or near intersections, at or just before railroad crossings, on narrow bridges, and anywhere passing is prohibited by signs or road markings.

question: If someone is tailgating you and there is an open lane to your right, you should:
options: a:Move over to the right lane if it is safe to do so.,b:Gradually reduce your speed immediately to force them to back off.,c:Brake suddenly to make them stop following you.
note: If someone is following too closely and there is a lane to your right, the safest response is to change to the right lane when it is safe and let them pass. If you cannot move over, gradually slow to increase following distance ahead and encourage the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this can cause a rear-end collision.

question: Which factor never affects a vehicle's stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,d:The condition and type of the road surface.
note: Stopping distance is affected by how quickly you react, your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the type and condition of the road surface, as well as weather and visibility. The time of day by itself does not change how far it takes your vehicle to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet oncoming traffic, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop always.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over.
note: On narrow roads, drivers meeting oncoming traffic must share the roadway so each vehicle has at least half of the main-traveled portion. This helps prevent sideswipe collisions and ensures both vehicles can pass safely without forcing one driver completely off the road.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When lights have stopped flashing.,c:When the train has already passed.,d:If the crossing is not busy.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates, even if you do not see a train or the train has just passed. Trains can come from either direction, and a second train may be approaching. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and signals indicate it is safe to proceed.

question: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means:
options: a:Speed limit.,b:Stop.,c:Hospital ahead.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it required to use your turn signal?
options: a:Whenever you turn, change lanes, pull into or out of a parking space, or enter traffic from a driveway, alley, or parking area.,b:Only when turning left.,c:Only when turning onto another street.
note: You are required to signal any time you turn, change lanes, or enter traffic from a parked position, driveway, alley, or parking area. Signaling well in advance lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you intend to do so they can adjust safely.

question: What should you do just before changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly turn your head without checking mirrors.,b:Check your side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,c:Only use your signal without checking behind you.,d:Signal after you begin the lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, first signal, then check your mirrors, and finally glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot. This sequence helps ensure there is no vehicle beside you that you cannot see in your mirrors.

question: A solid white edge line that slants toward the left indicates:
options: a:The road is narrowing ahead.,b:An intersection is coming up.,c:A construction zone immediately ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the roadway. When that right edge line begins to angle or slant toward the center of the road, it is warning you that the usable roadway is getting narrower ahead, so you should be prepared to adjust your position and speed.

question: If you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.,b:Proceed without stopping if no other vehicles are present.,c:Come to a full stop, yield as required, and proceed when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection, yield the right-of-way to any traffic or pedestrians already there, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which of the following can impair driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol, any medication, or lack of sleep.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol.
note: Driving ability can be reduced by alcohol, by both legal and illegal drugs (including some prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines), and by fatigue or lack of sleep. Any of these can slow your reactions, affect judgment, and make it unsafe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on major highways, what should you do to avoid 'highway hypnosis' and be prepared for hazards?
options: a:Stay alert and avoid staring at any one thing for more than a few seconds.,b:Keep your eyes fixed on the center of the road at all times.,c:Turn off your headlights in bright daylight.
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and let your mind drift, reducing your awareness of hazards. To prevent it, stay alert, keep your eyes moving, regularly scan mirrors and the road ahead, and avoid staring at any one spot for more than a few seconds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left side mirror.,b:Glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Only look in the rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, known as blind spots. Before changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle is in that blind spot.

question: What should you do on slippery roads?
options: a:Drive more quickly to pass hazardous patches.,b:Use cruise control for steady speed.,c:Slow down.,d:Maintain the posted speed limit no matter what.
note: On slippery roads, you must reduce your speed so your tires can maintain traction and you have more time to react. Rain, snow, or ice greatly increase stopping distance, so it is often necessary to drive slower than the posted speed limit to stay in control.

question: When passing on a multilane highway, you must:
options: a:Ensure the passing lane is clear, signal, and check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.,b:Always pass only on the right, even when a left passing lane is available.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction when passing on a multilane divided highway.
note: When passing on a multilane highway, you must use the left lane for passing (unless signs or conditions allow otherwise), make sure the lane is clear, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, then move over smoothly. You do not watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction because traffic in your direction is separated by lanes.

question: When sharing the road with a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist?
options: a:The use of a complete lane.,b:The use of half a lane only.,c:The use of the shoulder alongside your vehicle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane, just like any other vehicle. You must not crowd them or try to ride side‑by‑side in the same lane; always allow the motorcyclist to use the entire lane for safe maneuvering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down immediately.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may not legally pass another vehicle from your lane. It marks a no‑passing zone for your direction because visibility or road conditions make passing unsafe.

question: If a fire engine is following you but not using its emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving normally; you do not need to clear a path.,b:Pull over and stop immediately.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: You are required to yield and clear a path only when an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without emergency signals, continue driving normally and obey all traffic laws; do not speed up or stop unnecessarily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: High speeds affect crashes by:
options: a:Greatly increasing stopping distances and severity of collisions.,b:Decreasing stopping distances.,c:Having no effect on crash severity.
note: Higher speeds mean your vehicle needs a much longer distance to stop because both reaction distance and braking distance increase. If a crash happens at higher speed, the force of impact is much greater, so injuries and damage are usually more severe.

question: When you hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you while driving, you should:
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop or, in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can safely get out of the way.,b:Stop immediately where you are.,c:Speed up to get away.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop. In very heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can pull to the right and create a clear path.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Only if you confirm a train is not close.,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:Never drive around or under a gate that is moving up or down.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a railroad gate while it is lowering, down, or rising. Flashing lights, bells, and gates mean a train is near, and trains cannot stop quickly. Wait until the gates are fully raised, the signals stop, and you can clearly see it is safe before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to freeway traffic, and merge at about the same speed traffic is moving.,b:Signal and expect freeway traffic to yield to you.,c:Enter slowly and stop if necessary.
note: Traffic already on the freeway has the right‑of‑way. Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed, signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and merge when there is a safe gap at about the same speed as freeway traffic.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?
options: a:You may drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,b:You must slow and prepare to stop.,c:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic.,d:You must yield to all turning vehicles.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe and if you are not prohibited by signs or signals. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what is the best action to take?
options: a:Get some coffee and continue driving.,b:Open the window and keep driving.,c:Stop driving and rest or change drivers.,d:Turn up the radio and drive faster.
note: Driving while tired is very dangerous because your reaction time and awareness drop, similar to driving under the influence. The safest choice is to get off the road and rest or switch drivers. Tricks like coffee, opening windows, or loud music may briefly make you feel more awake, but they do not restore alertness and are not safe substitutes for rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition is passing another vehicle permitted?
options: a:When you are on a hill or in a curve because the view is usually clear.,b:By driving onto the shoulder of the road.,c:When the center line next to your lane is a broken yellow line and the passing lane ahead is clear.,d:Across a solid yellow line whenever traffic is light.
note: You may pass another vehicle only where passing is allowed by road markings and only when it is safe. A broken yellow line next to your lane means you are allowed to pass if the lane ahead is clear and you can complete the pass safely. Passing on hills, curves, shoulders, or across a solid yellow line is unsafe and generally illegal because you cannot see or use the lane properly.

question: As alcohol levels in your blood increase, what effect occurs?
options: a:Your reaction time slows down.,b:You become less confident.,c:The alcohol metabolizes itself faster.
note: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, your reaction time slows, your judgment and coordination worsen, and you often feel more confident even though your driving ability is reduced. This is why even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, which should drivers obey?
options: a:The traffic signal lights only.,b:The directions given by the officer.,c:Honking to alert the officer.,d:Traffic signs posted nearby rather than the officer's directions.
note: When a police officer or authorized person is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions override traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s directions, even if the traffic signal shows something different, to keep traffic moving safely and avoid conflicts.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, drivers:
options: a:May turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Must stop and wait for a solid green light.,c:Should treat it as a caution and merge into that lane.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed to turn after making sure the intersection is clear and yielding to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection. You do not need to stop first, but you must still use caution and be in the correct lane for the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, you should:
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge into a gap.,b:Enter far below highway speed and expect others to adjust.,c:Stop at the ramp end and then enter slowly.
note: When entering a highway, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and merge into a safe gap. You must yield to vehicles already on the highway and avoid entering much slower than traffic, which can cause rear-end collisions.

question: What should a driver do after taking an over-the-counter medication before driving?
options: a:Double the dose to stay alert.,b:Drink alcohol to offset side effects.,c:Read the medication label for warnings about driving.,d:Ignore the label and drive as usual.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read the label for warnings about driving or operating machinery, and if you are unsure or feel affected, do not drive and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

question: What is a good general rule about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to improve visibility.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe.
note: Passing always carries extra risk because it puts you in or near oncoming traffic and blind spots. It is safer to travel with the flow of traffic and only pass when it is legal, necessary, and you have enough clear space to complete the maneuver safely.

question: When driving in fog you should use which lights?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In fog, high beams reflect off the water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Use low beam headlights so you can see the road and be seen by others without increasing glare, and slow down to match visibility conditions.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to:
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely.,b:Pull next to them and shout.,c:Flash your high beams at them.
note: If another driver cuts you off, reacting aggressively increases the chance of a crash or road rage incident. The safest response is to stay calm, slow slightly if needed to re-establish a safe following distance, and continue driving defensively.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Red lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Black lines.,d:White lines.
note: Yellow lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and red or black are not used for this purpose.

question: Which of the following is a common source of distracted driving?
options: a:Checking tire pressure while driving.,b:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,c:Changing the oil before driving.
note: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes at least one hand and some of your attention away from the road, making it a common source of distracted driving. Vehicle maintenance tasks like checking tire pressure or changing oil are done when the vehicle is not moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:The maximum posted speed limit only.,b:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:A speed that is safe for existing conditions regardless of posted limits.
note: You must always drive at a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions, even if this means driving slower than the posted speed limit. Driving faster than is safe for conditions is illegal, even when you are below the posted limit.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive and may result in DUII?
options: a:Alcoholic beverages such as beer, wine, or liquor.,b:Controlled substances and certain prescription medicines.,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,d:All of the above.
note: Any substance that affects your judgment, coordination, or reaction time can impair driving. Alcohol, illegal drugs, some prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines, and inhalants like glue or paint can all lead to a DUII charge if they impair your ability to drive safely.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign indicates:
options: a:A road hazard or warning.,b:An interstate route.,c:A school crossing.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to specific road hazards or changes ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings, so you can adjust your driving in advance.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Assume it operates like any other vehicle.,b:Hide defects from the owner to avoid embarrassment.,c:Take a few minutes to locate and test the controls and check for defects.
note: Before driving any unfamiliar vehicle, take a few minutes to adjust the seat and mirrors, locate and test the lights, wipers, turn signals, horn, and brakes, and check for any obvious defects. Do not drive the vehicle if you find a safety problem until it is corrected.

question: When should you slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:Only when a police officer tells you to.,c:Only when passing another vehicle.
note: You must slow down whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop, such as on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on steep hills or blind curves, and when the road is wet, icy, or otherwise slippery. Speed must always be adjusted to conditions, not just signs or police direction.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, or before entering the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed if clear.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present.
note: A steady red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop before the stop line, before entering a crosswalk, or before entering the intersection if there is no line or crosswalk. You must remain stopped until the light turns green or you are otherwise directed to proceed, such as by a green arrow or a police officer.

question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, you should:
options: a:Stop for a rest every two hours.,b:Drive faster to finish earlier.,c:Do arm exercises while driving.
note: To prevent fatigue on long trips, plan to stop at least every two hours to get out, walk around, and rest your eyes and mind. If you feel drowsy at any time, pull over in a safe place and rest; do not try to fight sleep by speeding up or doing exercises while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space required to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Whether a stop sign is present.,c:Whether you have signaled.
note: The time and space needed to cross traffic safely depend on how quickly you can accelerate, the speed and distance of oncoming traffic, and road and weather conditions that affect traction and visibility. You must allow enough gap so you can clear the intersection without forcing other drivers to slow or swerve.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop whether a stop sign is present or not.,c:Sound your horn to alert children.
note: At a school crossing sign, you must slow down, watch carefully for children who may enter the road unexpectedly, and be ready to stop whenever children or a crossing guard are present. You are not required to stop every time you see the sign, only when pedestrians are in or about to enter the crosswalk or when directed by a crossing guard or signal.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:You should check antifreeze and washer fluid levels more often.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Snow tires can increase traction on slippery surfaces.
note: In winter, roads can be icy or snow-covered, making traction and stopping distances worse. You should check antifreeze and washer fluid more often, and snow tires can improve traction. Cruise control should not be used on snow, ice, or in similar hazardous conditions because it can cause you to lose control if the vehicle starts to skid.

question: What best ensures safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Honk your horn before shifting to reverse.,b:Check behind the vehicle by walking to the rear before getting in the driver's seat.,c:Rely only on rearview mirrors and cameras.,d:Back quickly to finish sooner.
note: The safest way to back is to first walk around the vehicle and check behind it for children, pedestrians, or objects you cannot see from the driver’s seat. Then back slowly while looking over your shoulder and using mirrors and cameras as aids, not as your only method of checking. Never rely solely on mirrors or cameras, and never back quickly.

question: What color lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Green lines.,d:Blue lines.
note: Yellow center lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. The pattern of yellow lines (solid or broken) tells you whether passing is allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes, you may cross to pass.,b:No, you may not cross to pass.,c:Yes, but only when making a left turn into or from a driveway or side road.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass other vehicles. You may carefully cross double solid yellow lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or when directed by law enforcement or traffic control. You must never use a double solid yellow line area as a passing zone.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster through standing water.,b:Drive through shallow water only.,c:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. The best way to reduce the risk is to slow down in wet conditions and avoid driving fast through standing water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a green light change to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution instead of braking hard.

question: Anything that causes you to which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,d:Any of the above.
note: Anything that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving is a distraction and can lead to a crash. Looking away, handling objects, or daydreaming all reduce your ability to react to hazards in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers permitted to text while operating a motor vehicle?
options: a:Yes, texting is allowed while driving.,b:No, texting is not permitted while driving.,c:Yes, but only if traffic is light.,d:Only when legally parked and not in a traffic lane.
note: You may not write, send, or read electronic messages while driving. This includes texts, emails, and internet use.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow displayed at an intersection mean?
options: a:The green arrow is coming next so speed up.,b:You may proceed in the arrow direction without yielding.,c:Slow to a stop if you can do so safely because a red arrow is coming.,d:The signal is malfunctioning.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, you may complete the turn with caution.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is permitted from either lane.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and not allowed for traffic on the side with the solid line. Drivers on the solid-line side must not cross it to pass.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving skills?
options: a:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can limit concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only a BAC above the legal limit impairs driving.,c:Alcohol does not affect driving at low doses.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect the brain and reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and reaction time. Even if you are below the legal BAC limit, your driving can still be impaired, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking.

question: If another driver aggressively cuts you off, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to show them they were wrong.,b:Call the police right away.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: When another driver cuts you off or behaves aggressively, stay calm, avoid eye contact, and safely create space between your vehicle and theirs. Do not retaliate or try to teach them a lesson, because that can quickly escalate into road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

question: Drowsy drivers may:
options: a:Safely continue by drinking coffee.,b:Drive so poorly they resemble intoxicated drivers.,c:Stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
note: Drowsy drivers often have slowed reactions, poor judgment, and trouble staying in their lane, which can make their driving resemble that of an intoxicated driver. Coffee, fresh air, or loud music are not reliable solutions—if you feel drowsy, the safe choice is to stop and rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always signal when which of the following actions is performed?
options: a:When turning, changing lanes, or entering or leaving a parking space or the curb.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Only when other vehicles are present.
note: Turn signals must be used whenever you change lanes, turn, or enter or leave traffic, including when parking or pulling away from a curb. You should signal even if you do not see other vehicles, because traffic can appear quickly and other road users, like pedestrians and cyclists, also rely on your signals.

question: Signs colored orange typically indicate what?
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Work zone signs.
note: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used in work zones. They alert drivers to construction, maintenance, or utility work and related hazards so drivers can slow down, be prepared to stop, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicates:
options: a:Decrease speed and yield the right-of-way to others.,b:Stop completely under all circumstances.,c:Always stop and honk before proceeding.
note: A red-and-white triangle is a yield sign. You must slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:A single broken yellow line.,b:A combination solid and broken yellow line.,c:A double solid yellow line.,d:A dashed white line.
note: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-way road means vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass. You must stay in your lane and may only cross when turning left where it is allowed and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, the safest practice is to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic rather than much faster or slower than others.,b:Drive much faster than surrounding traffic to avoid congestion.,c:Drive much slower than others to be safer.
note: Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of crashes. The safest practice is to travel with the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit and adjusting for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through if no other traffic is present.,b:Come to a complete stop and then proceed only as permitted.,c:Speed through to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Ignore it if turning is allowed without signage.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line. After stopping, you may proceed straight or turn only when the signal allows and where turns on red are legal, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To change lanes safely, what sequence should you follow?
options: a:Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes without looking over your shoulder.,b:Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.,c:Signal and change lanes immediately.
note: The safe lane-change sequence is: signal first to communicate your intention, check your mirrors, then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and change lanes only if it is clear. Relying only on mirrors is unsafe because vehicles can be hidden in blind spots.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to beat any approaching train.,c:Drive around any lowered gate if traffic backs up.,d:Ignore unmarked crossings.
note: When approaching any railroad crossing, you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Never speed up to beat a train, never drive around lowered gates, and do not ignore unmarked crossings—trains can use any track at any time.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Directly at the headlights.,b:Toward the left side of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road.,d:At the center line.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare from the headlights while still letting you track your lane position and see the road ahead.

question: When must you turn on your headlights in Massachusetts tunnels?
options: a:Only during nighttime hours.,b:Only if visibility is poor.,c:Always when driving in a tunnel.
note: In Massachusetts, you must turn on your headlights whenever you drive in a tunnel, regardless of time of day or weather. Headlights make it easier for you to see and for other drivers to see you in the reduced light of a tunnel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you go through an intersection controlled by a stop sign but there is no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing down and checking there is no cross traffic.,b:Only after coming to a full stop before entering the intersection and verifying it is safe to proceed.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: At a stop-sign-controlled intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection—typically just before the point where you would enter the cross traffic. Proceed only after checking that the way is clear and it is safe.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:Can be ticketed just like a motor vehicle driver.,b:Has special immunity and cannot be ticketed.,c:Will always be warned but not cited.
note: Bicyclists generally must follow the same traffic laws as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey signals, signs, and right‑of‑way rules, and they can receive tickets for violations such as running red lights or stop signs.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should steer:
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid and hold it.,c:Keep the front wheels straight at all costs.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, you should look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. As the vehicle begins to straighten out, be ready to steer as needed to keep control and avoid overcorrecting.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Using turn signals properly.,b:Keeping a steady following distance.,c:Driving exactly at the speed limit.,d:Weaving between lanes.
note: A common sign of an impaired or drunk driver is weaving or drifting between lanes. Other warning signs include inconsistent speeds, sudden stops, and poor lane control. If you see this behavior, stay well back and, when safe, report it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When passing another car.,b:To alert others when you must stop quickly.,c:Whenever you are frustrated with another driver.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as when you must stop or slow suddenly and need to alert drivers or pedestrians. Do not use the horn to express anger or without a safety reason.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Exit at the next exit and safely return to your intended exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the interstate.,c:Roll down your window and ask another driver for directions.
