note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, continue to the next exit, then find a safe route back. Never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the interstate, as this is extremely dangerous and illegal.

question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must be obeyed?
options: a:White.,b:Blue.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do (such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way signs). In the U.S., they are most often white with black or red lettering or symbols, and they must always be obeyed because they communicate traffic laws.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No,b:Yes,c:You yes
note: Open container laws in all states make it illegal to drink alcohol or have an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road. Neither the driver nor passengers may legally drink while the vehicle is on a public highway, even if the driver is not over the legal BAC limit.

question: “Highway hypnosis” is most likely caused by:
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning.,b:Taking frequent rest stops.,c:Getting too much sleep before the trip.,d:Listening to loud music.
note: Highway hypnosis is a trance-like state that can occur on long, monotonous drives when you stare straight ahead and stop actively scanning your surroundings. To prevent it, move your eyes regularly, check mirrors often, take breaks, and stay mentally engaged with the driving task.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed and turn.,b:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic in the intersection.,c:Stop only if a police officer is present.,d:Signal after you start the turn.
note: A green light means you may turn right if it is safe, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or close to the intersection. You must also signal before turning and obey any signs that prohibit or restrict the turn.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass trucks or buses.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Flash your headlights at them to get their attention.
note: Trucks and buses have large blind spots directly behind them and along both sides, especially on the right. To stay visible, avoid driving alongside them for long periods and do not follow too closely. Pass promptly and safely, and leave extra space so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway you should begin slowing:
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road before the exit lane.,c:Only when you see the toll booth.
note: On highways you should maintain the normal traffic speed on the main roadway and only begin slowing after you have safely moved into the exit lane or ramp. Slowing on the main road before the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of rear‑end collisions.

question: When a flagger is controlling traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore the flagger and follow other drivers.,b:Assume the flagger isn't authorized to direct traffic.,c:Follow the flagger's directions.
note: Flaggers in construction zones are authorized to direct traffic and their instructions have the same legal force as traffic signals or signs. You must watch for them, be prepared to slow or stop, and follow their directions to keep workers and drivers safe.

question: The act of turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit.,c:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,d:Only required for new drivers.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot fully cover. Turning your head briefly to check your blind spot before changing lanes is a good and necessary driving habit to make sure there are no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles beside you.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach.,b:Body weight of the individual.,c:How much time passes between drinks.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol’s effect depends on several factors, including how much you drink, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and whether you have food in your stomach. These factors influence your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and how impaired you become.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:You are traveling much faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic might not see you pull out to pass the bicyclist.
note: You should be cautious when passing a bicyclist because you are usually traveling much faster and need extra time and space to pass safely. Bicyclists can be unstable, may need to swerve to avoid hazards, and you must leave a safe clearance—often at least 3 feet or more where required by law—before moving back into the lane.

question: Which of the following will help you sober up quickly after drinking?
options: a:A cold shower.,b:A large coffee.,c:Exercising.,d:None of the above; only time will sober you.
note: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol concentration. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise may make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how quickly your body processes alcohol. You must allow enough time for the alcohol to leave your system before driving.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and no passing is allowed.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so. Opposing directions of travel are separated by yellow lines, not white.

question: About speed management when navigating curves, you should:
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve.,b:Maintain posted speed until the sharpest part, then slow.,c:Accelerate gently into the curve.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve, then maintain a safe, steady speed through it. Braking hard in the middle of a curve can cause you to lose traction and control because of inertia and reduced tire grip while turning.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The medicine will block the alcohol's effects.,b:Alcohol will help the medicine work faster.,c:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of both substances.
note: Alcohol can interact with both prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines to greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, and slowed reaction time. This combination can impair driving much more than alcohol or the medicine alone and can be very dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While in a travel lane on the roadway, which is true?
options: a:You may stop briefly to drop off passengers.,b:You should keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.,c:You may make a U-turn if you missed an entrance ramp.
note: Travel lanes are for moving traffic. You should not stop in a travel lane except in an emergency. If you miss a turn or exit, keep driving until you reach a safe place to pull off the road or turn around, rather than stopping or backing up in the lane.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Because visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars overheat more often at night.,c:It rains more at night.
note: Night driving is harder because your visibility is reduced: you see less of the road ahead and to the sides, and it’s harder to judge distance and speed. You should slow down and use your headlights correctly so you can stop within the distance you can see.

question: If you are in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Ignore the scene and continue driving.,b:Drive away if the damage seems minor.,c:Argue with the other driver before exchanging information.,d:Determine if anyone is injured and call emergency services if needed.
note: After a serious crash, you must stop, protect the scene, and check for injuries. Your first priority is safety: determine if anyone is hurt and call 911 if needed. If vehicles can be moved and it is safe, move them out of traffic, then exchange information and make any legally required reports.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and keep driving.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches on a one‑way street, you must pull toward the nearest edge or curb—right or left—and stop until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: When driving in fog, you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, use low‑beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can create glare, making it even harder to see. Parking lights alone are not enough for you to see or be seen.

question: Which actions should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal your lane change only.,b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors only.,c:Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,d:Change lanes without signaling if you can do it quickly.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, signal to let others know your intention, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This sequence helps ensure there is enough space and that no vehicle is hidden beside you.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Move the injured person immediately to clear traffic.,b:Always leave the injured where they are and wait.,c:Avoid moving the injured unless necessary, keep them warm, and give first aid if trained.
note: Avoid moving an injured person unless there is immediate danger, such as fire or risk of another collision. Unnecessary movement can worsen neck, back, or internal injuries. Call 911, keep the person warm and as still as possible, and only give first aid if you are trained, staying with them until emergency services arrive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:Only during daytime.,b:On hills and curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,c:Only when pavement is wet.,d:Only in school zones.
note: Passing is generally prohibited where your view is limited or conflicts are likely, such as on hills and curves where you cannot see oncoming traffic, at intersections where vehicles or pedestrians may enter, and at railroad crossings where trains may approach. Always obey no-passing signs and pavement markings that also restrict passing.

question: What should you remember about wet pavement and rain?
options: a:Wet roads cannot cause hydroplaning.,b:You should always tailgate to increase control.,c:Pavement is especially slippery right after rain begins.
note: When rain first begins, water mixes with oil, grease, and dirt on the road surface, making it especially slippery. During this time you should slow down, avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and increase your following distance to reduce the risk of skidding or hydroplaning.

question: You are in the left lane and want to move right. Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check mirrors and your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Look in mirrors only.,c:Only signal and change lanes without checking blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes to the right, you must check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly glance over your right shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in your blind spots, so a shoulder check is essential to be sure the lane is clear before you move.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when which of the following occurs?
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger.,b:The crossing is controlled by a stop sign.,c:Flashing red signals or lowered gates are present and operating.,d:Any of the above.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time warning devices indicate a train is coming, such as flashing red lights, lowered gates, or a flagger’s signal. You also must stop when there is a stop sign at the crossing, even if no train is visible, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which statement about advisory speed signs on curves is correct?
options: a:They are blue with black lettering.,b:You should reduce speed before entering the curve as indicated.,c:They can be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,d:They are triangular in shape.
note: Advisory speed signs on curves are yellow with black lettering and show a recommended safe speed for ideal conditions. You should slow to about that speed before entering the curve, because braking hard while turning can cause loss of control, especially on slippery roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best practice?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.,b:Proceed slowly and wait for an opening at low speed.,c:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and blend in.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on‑ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic already on the freeway, then merge into a suitable gap. Entering too slowly or stopping at the end of the ramp can surprise other drivers and increase the risk of a collision.

question: Which action is illegal at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Stopping when directed by a flagger.,b:Waiting for a train to pass.,c:Driving around lowered gates.,d:Obeying flashing lights and gates.
note: At railroad crossings you must always obey flashing lights, gates, and any flagger. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around lowered gates because a train may be approaching or there may be a second train you cannot see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle that honks first.,d:The vehicle going straight if the other is turning.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. If you see another vehicle coming from your right, allow that driver to go first to prevent confusion and collisions.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement indicates that drivers in that lane:
options: a:May choose to make the movement but are not required to.,b:Must make the movement shown by the arrow.,c:Must stop before making the movement.,d:Should yield to traffic in the oncoming lane.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement show what movement is required from that lane, such as turn only or straight only, unless a sign or signal indicates otherwise. You must follow the direction of the arrow to keep traffic organized and avoid conflicts.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory road signs?
options: a:They warn of present dangers ahead.,b:They indicate what a driver must or must not do.,c:They are always diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,d:They show nearby services and distances.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as obeying speed limits, stopping at stop signs, or not turning where prohibited. They are usually rectangular with black, white, or red symbols or words, and they are legally enforceable.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Ignore the signal and continue normally.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield and carefully check for other traffic, pedestrians, or hazards before going through the intersection.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:When the bus is stopped and its red lights are flashing.,b:Only when the bus is in your lane and doors are open.,c:Only if the bus driver signals you to stop.
note: On a two-lane road with no median, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and/or stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving much slower than the speed limit and causing backup, what should you do?
options: a:Continue at the slow speed because it is safest.,b:Always expect the right-of-way.,c:Pull off the road when safe to allow other vehicles to pass.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or make sudden lane changes. If you are traveling well below the speed of traffic and creating a backup, you should pull off the road at a safe place and allow other vehicles to pass.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, what is the safest response?
options: a:Take no special action and continue.,b:Slow down and pass the animal carefully to avoid startling it.,c:Pass the animal as closely as possible to get by quickly.
note: When you see an animal on or near the roadway, slow down and pass very carefully. Sudden movements, loud engine noise, or passing too close can startle the animal and cause it to move unpredictably into your path, increasing the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by double solid yellow lines, you may:
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass another vehicle when no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Never cross under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean you may not cross them to pass another vehicle. However, you are allowed to carefully cross double solid yellow lines to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic near a school, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore the guard if a traffic signal is present.,b:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.,c:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,d:Do whatever surrounding traffic does even if it contradicts the guard.
note: You must always obey a crossing guard’s instructions in a school zone, even if traffic signals or other signs are present. Crossing guards are authorized to control traffic to protect children and pedestrians, and their directions override normal signal indications when they are actively directing traffic.

question: What is the minimum auto liability insurance coverage for property damage required for motor vehicles registered in Massachusetts for policies written or renewed on or after July 1, 2025?
note: Effective July 1, 2025, Massachusetts increased the mandatory minimum property damage liability coverage from $5,000 to $30,000 per accident.

question: Under Massachusetts law, within how many days must a driver file a Motor Vehicle Crash Operator Report if an accident results in injury, death, or property damage exceeding $1,000?
options: a:24 hours,b:3 days,c:5 days,d:10 days
note: In Massachusetts, you must file a written crash report with both the RMV and local police department within five days of an accident that causes injury, death, or property damage exceeding $1,000.
